title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a categorical variable, each category becomes a separate binary column. For example, if you one-hot encode the 'sex' column, you will have two new columns: $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$.

title: Columns in the Design Matrix
text: After one-hot encoding 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$, how many columns will you have in total? Remember, each category in a column becomes a separate column in the design matrix.

title: Checking Full Column Rank
text: A matrix is full column rank if all its columns are linearly independent. Consider if any column can be expressed as a linear combination of others.

title: Calculating the Number of Columns
text: How many columns will the design matrix have after one-hot encoding 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$?

title: Determining Linear Independence
text: Are there any columns in the design matrix that can be expressed as a linear combination of others?
